items.answer: Decomposition

items.answer: wind

items.answer: Hans Christian Oersted

items.markingKey: (b) The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, i.e. 15° per hour; 8 × 15 = 120°.

items.answer: Magnetic force

items.stem: Arrange these organisms in a correct food chain: leaves, sparrow, caterpillar, cat. Identify the producer and the top consumer.
items.answer: leaves → caterpillar → sparrow → cat; producer: leaves; top consumer: cat
items.markingKey: Energy flows from the plant upwards: leaves → caterpillar → sparrow → cat (1 mark); producer and top consumer (1 mark).

items.stem: Does diffuse reflection mean that the laws of reflection are not obeyed? Explain.
items.answer: No. Each ray obeys the laws; the surface is rough, so normals at different points point in different directions and the reflected rays spread out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: laws obeyed. 1 mark: normals differ.

items.stem: Why should we not take shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm?
items.answer: Lightning tends to strike tall objects; the current can pass through the tree to a person standing nearby.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: tall objects struck. 1 mark: danger to person.

items.stem: Why is the female Anopheles mosquito called a vector?
items.answer: It carries the malaria parasite from an infected person to a healthy person while sucking blood.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: carrier. 1 mark: transfers pathogen.

items.stem: Two cups of tea look different in colour. What does this tell you about their concentrations?
items.answer: The darker cup has more dissolved tea (solute) per amount of water, so it is more concentrated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: more solute. 1 mark: concentration.

items.stem: Aarav made a conduction tester with a cell, a bulb and two free wire ends, and touched the free ends to each of these in turn: silver spoon, rubber band, paper, copper wire. For which objects will the bulb glow? Give a reason.
items.answer: Bulb glows for copper wire, silver spoon; not for paper, rubber band.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: correct list. 1 mark: silver spoon, copper wire are conductors and complete the circuit; the others are insulators.

items.stem: Aditya has a mass of 54 kg. Find Aditya's weight on the Earth and on the Moon (g = 9.8 m/s²; gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth). What is the mass on the Moon?
items.answer: Earth: 529.2 N; Moon: about 88.2 N; mass stays 54 kg.
items.markingKey: W = 54 × 9.8 = 529.2 N; on Moon 529.2 ÷ 6 ≈ 88.2 N; mass does not change.

items.stem: Draw a labelled diagram of a plant cell (describe it in words) and mark the parts not found in animal cells.
items.answer: Labelled parts: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chloroplasts, large vacuole. Cell wall, chloroplasts and large vacuole are absent in animal cells.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: correct labels; 1 mark: parts absent in animal cells identified.

items.stem: Manish heated naphthalene from 57 °C and recorded the temperature every minute. The temperature rose steadily, stayed at 80 °C for 4 minutes, and then rose again. (i) What is the melting point? (ii) Why did the temperature stay constant? (iii) What is the state of the substance during the constant part?
items.answer: (i) 80 °C. (ii) Heat was used to overcome interparticle attraction (melting), not to raise temperature. (iii) A mixture of solid and liquid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: A school roof in Chennai has an area of 100 m² and the city receives 1500 mm of rain in a year. About how many litres of rainwater could be harvested in a year? (1 m³ = 1000 L)
items.answer: 150000 litres
items.markingKey: Volume = area × rainfall = 100 m² × 1.5 m = 150 m³ = 150000 L.

items.stem: Plan a fair test to find how the height of a ramp affects how far a toy car rolls. Name the variable you will change, the variable you will measure and any two variables you will keep the same.
items.answer: Change: height of the ramp. Measure: distance rolled by the car. Keep the same: the same toy car and surface of the floor (also length of the ramp).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: independent variable, dependent variable, two controlled variables.

items.stem: In the food chain mango leaves → insect → lizard → snake, the mango leaves store 5 000 J of energy. If only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, how much energy reaches the snake?
items.answer: 5 J

items.stem: A ray of light makes an angle of 40° with the surface of a plane mirror. Find the angle of incidence and the angle between the incident and reflected rays.
items.answer: Angle of incidence 50°; angle between rays 100°
items.markingKey: Angles are measured from the normal: i = 90° − 40° = 50°; r = 50°; angle between rays = 50 + 50 = 100°.

items.stem:
Read: Dev, of weight 400 N, stands in soft snow in Gulmarg. The total area of the soles of the boots is 0.02 m², and the total area of a pair of skis is 0.4 m².
(i) Find the pressure on the snow with boots. (ii) Find the pressure with skis. (iii) In which case will Dev sink less, and why? (iv) Give one other example where a larger area is used to reduce pressure.
items.answer: (i) 20000 Pa. (ii) 1000 Pa. (iii) With skis: the same weight acts on a larger area, so pressure is less. (iv) Wide straps of school bags / broad tyres of tractors / camel's broad feet.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: A health survey of 400 families in Patna after the monsoon recorded the percentage of families with at least one case of: tuberculosis – 10%; dengue – 12%; typhoid – 40%.
(i) How many families reported typhoid? (ii) How does typhoid spread? (iii) Which of these diseases are caused by bacteria? (iv) Suggest one measure the municipal body should take for typhoid.
items.answer: (i) 40% of 400 = 160. (ii) Through contaminated food and water. (iii) tuberculosis, typhoid. (iv) Supply chlorinated drinking water and check food sold in the open.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: Rahul made an electromagnet with an iron nail and one cell and counted the pins it could hold for different numbers of turns: 10 turns – 3 pins; 20 turns – 7 pins; 30 turns – 9 pins; 40 turns – 13 pins.
(i) What is the independent variable? (ii) What pattern do you see? (iii) Predict the number of pins for 50 turns. (iv) Suggest one other way to make it stronger.
items.answer: (i) Number of turns. (ii) More turns, more pins (stronger electromagnet). (iii) About 15 pins. (iv) Increase the current by using more cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Explain how the rotation and revolution of the Earth give us the day and the year. Why do we have seasons? Describe what happens on 21 June and 22 December in the northern hemisphere.
items.answer: Rotation on its tilted axis in ~24 h gives day and night; revolution around the Sun in ~365¼ days gives the year. Seasons occur because the axis is tilted 23.5°, so each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight and longer days when tilted towards the Sun. 21 June: longest day, summer solstice in the north. 22 December: shortest day, winter solstice.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: rotation and revolution; 1 mark: seasons; 2 marks: solstices.

items.stem: Distinguish between contact and non-contact forces with two examples each. Explain why a ball thrown up comes back down and why the ball stops when it rolls on the ground.
items.answer: Contact forces act only on touching (muscular force, friction); non-contact forces act from a distance (magnetic, electrostatic, gravitational). A ball comes down because gravity pulls it; a rolling ball stops because friction opposes its motion.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: distinction with examples; 1.5 marks each explanation.

items.stem: Explain with examples how microorganisms can harm (a) human beings, (b) plants and (c) our food. Describe any two methods of preserving food and how each works.
items.answer: (a) Cause diseases such as cholera, typhoid (bacteria), common cold (virus), malaria (protozoa). (b) Citrus canker (bacteria), rust of wheat (fungi), yellow vein mosaic of bhindi (virus). (c) Spoil food and cause food poisoning by producing toxins. Preservation: salting removes water; pasteurisation (70 °C for 15–30 s, then chilled) kills microbes; refrigeration slows their growth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for (a), (b), (c); 1 mark each for two preservation methods with reason.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Small steel balls placed between moving parts to replace sliding with rolling friction."
items.answer: ball bearings
items.markingKey: (b) Ball bearings is small steel balls placed between moving parts to replace sliding with rolling friction.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A solution that contains a small amount of solute in a large amount of solvent."
items.answer: a dilute solution

items.answer: citrus canker

items.stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
items.answer: copper wire
items.markingKey: (c) Copper wire is a good conductor of electricity. The others: rubber band – an insulator; cotton thread – an insulator; dry wood – an insulator.

items.answer: A condition in which the blood sugar level stays high because the body does not make or use insulin properly

items.answer: one-sixth

items.answer: a solute

items.stem: An Amoeba keeps changing its shape. Explain why.
items.answer: It has no rigid cell wall; it pushes out finger-like pseudopodia to move and capture food.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: no cell wall. 1 mark: pseudopodia for movement/feeding.

items.stem: Give one advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet.
items.answer: Its magnetism can be switched on and off, and its strength can be changed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: switchable. 1 mark: adjustable strength.

items.stem: Why is regular exercise good for the heart?
items.answer: It strengthens the heart muscle, helps control weight and blood pressure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: strengthens heart. 1 mark: controls weight/BP.

items.stem: Why is "Which flower is the prettiest?" not a scientific question?
items.answer: Its answer depends on personal opinion; it cannot be tested or measured with evidence.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: depends on opinion/taste. 1 mark: cannot be tested or measured.

items.stem: Why should we use public transport, bicycles or car pools?
items.answer: They save petrol and diesel, which are non-renewable, and reduce air pollution.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: saves fossil fuel. 1 mark: less pollution.

items.stem: Why is it correct to say "the mass of the bag is 5 kg" but not "the weight of the bag is 5 kg"?
items.answer: Mass is measured in kilograms; weight is a force and is measured in newtons (about 49 N for 5 kg).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: mass in kg. 1 mark: weight in N.

items.stem: A glass marble has a mass of 260 g and a volume of 100 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.answer: 2.6 g/cm³; it will sink
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 260 ÷ 100 = 2.6 g/cm³; more than water, so it sinks.

items.stem: A brick of weight 20 N measures 0.2 m × 0.1 m × 0.05 m. Find the largest and smallest pressure it can exert on the ground, and say which face it rests on each time.
items.answer: Largest 4000 Pa on the 0.1 m × 0.05 m face; smallest 1000 Pa on the 0.2 m × 0.1 m face.
items.markingKey: Smallest area 0.005 m² gives P = 20 ÷ 0.005 = 4000 Pa; largest area 0.02 m² gives 1000 Pa. 1 mark each area, 1 mark each pressure, 1 mark faces.

A ray of light makes an angle of 30° with the surface of a plane mirror. Find the angle of incidence and the angle between the incident and reflected rays.
items.answer: Angle of incidence 60°; angle between rays 120°
items.markingKey: Angles are measured from the normal: i = 90° − 30° = 60°; r = 60°; angle between rays = 60 + 60 = 120°.

items.stem: Ishaan heated wax from 32 °C and recorded the temperature every minute. The temperature rose steadily, stayed at 55 °C for 4 minutes, and then rose again. (i) What is the melting point? items.answer: (i) 55 °C. (ii) Heat was used to overcome interparticle attraction (melting), not to raise temperature. (iii) A mixture of solid and liquid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: A shopkeeper in a hilly town says he does not need to keep his jams in a refrigerator, but he keeps paneer in it. Justify his choice.
items.answer: Jam has a high sugar content, so microbes cannot grow; paneer is moist and rich in protein and spoils quickly unless kept cold.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sugar preserves jam. 1 mark: paneer perishable, needs cold.

items.stem: A torch does not glow even with new cells. List three faults you would check and explain why each would stop the torch from working.
items.answer: Cells put in the wrong way (circuit does not work); fused bulb (broken filament breaks the circuit); loose or rusted switch/spring contact (open circuit).
items.markingKey: 1 mark per fault with reason.

items.stem:
Read: A health survey of 200 families in Patna after the monsoon recorded the percentage of families with at least one case of: malaria – 10%; common cold – 24%; dengue – 40%.
(i) How many families reported dengue? (ii) How does dengue spread? (iii) Which of these diseases are caused by bacteria? (iv) Suggest one measure the municipal body should take for dengue.
items.answer: (i) 40% of 200 = 80. (ii) Through mosquito bites. (iii) none of them. (iv) Remove stagnant water from coolers, tyres and pots, and spray larvicide.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: A class recorded the time taken for 5 g of sugar to dissolve in 100 mL of water at different temperatures: 10 °C – 193 s; 50 °C – 172 s; 60 °C – 155 s; 70 °C – 139 s. (i) Name the independent and dependent variables. (ii) What pattern do you see? (iii) Predict the time at a temperature higher than 70 °C.
items.answer: (i) Independent: water temperature; dependent: time to dissolve. (ii) The higher the temperature, the less time sugar takes to dissolve. (iii) Less than 139 s.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: A school in Bengaluru plans rooftop rainwater harvesting. The roof area is 80 m² and the yearly rainfall is 800 mm. The school uses about 2000 L of water a day.
(i) How much rainwater (in litres) can be collected in a year? (1 m² × 1 mm = 1 L) (ii) For about how many days would it meet the school's needs? (iii) Is rainwater a renewable resource? (iv) Give one way to use the water other than storing it in tanks.
items.answer: (i) 64000 L. (ii) About 32 days. (iii) Yes. (iv) Lead it into a recharge pit to raise the groundwater level.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: What is friction? Explain two factors on which it depends. Describe two ways of increasing and two ways of reducing friction, with one example each.
items.answer: Friction is the force opposing relative motion between surfaces in contact. It depends on the nature of the surfaces (rough surfaces give more) and how hard they are pressed together (heavier objects, more friction). Increase: treads on tyres, sand on slippery roads. Reduce: lubricants such as oil, ball bearings/wheels, polishing, streamlining.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 2 marks: factors; 2 marks: ways with examples.

items.stem: Explain the terms solute, solvent, saturated solution and concentration with examples. Calculate the mass of salt needed to make 250 g of a 4% (mass by mass) salt solution, and the mass of water.
items.answer: Solute: substance that dissolves (salt); solvent: substance in which it dissolves (water); saturated: no more solute dissolves at that temperature; concentration: amount of solute in a given amount of solution. Salt = 4 × 250 ÷ 100 = 10 g; water = 240 g.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: terms; 2 marks: calculation.

items.stem: Explain how a thunderstorm and a cyclone are formed. Describe the structure of a cyclone and list three safety measures to be taken during a cyclone.
items.answer: Thunderstorm: warm moist air rises rapidly, cools, forms tall clouds with lightning and thunder. Cyclone: over warm seas, warm moist air rises, condensation releases heat, low pressure deepens, winds spiral in. Structure: calm low-pressure eye surrounded by a wall of strong winds and heavy rain. Safety: follow IMD warnings, move to shelters, store food and water, avoid going to sea.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: thunderstorm; 2 marks: cyclone formation and eye; 2 marks: safety.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface."

items.stem: A food web is more stable than a single food chain because:

options: animals have other food choices if one is lost

items.stem: In soda water, the solute is:
items.answer: carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: (a) Carbon dioxide dissolves in water; so carbon dioxide is the solute and water the solvent.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The force exerted by a charged object on another charged or uncharged object."
items.answer: electrostatic force
items.markingKey: (a) Electrostatic force is the force exerted by a charged object on another charged or uncharged object.

items.stem: What is meant by a deficiency disease?
items.answer: A disease caused by the lack of a nutrient in the diet over a long time
items.markingKey: (d) A disease caused by the lack of a nutrient in the diet over a long time. 1 mark: A deficiency disease – a disease caused by the lack of a nutrient in the diet over a long time.
options: A diet that contains all nutrients in the right amounts along with roughage and water
A state of physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease
Dietary fibre from plant foods that helps the body get rid of undigested food
A disease caused by the lack of a nutrient in the diet over a long time

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The spinning of the Earth on its axis from west to east, completed in about 24 hours."
items.answer: rotation of the Earth
items.markingKey: (b) Rotation of the Earth is the spinning of the Earth on its axis from west to east, completed in about 24 hours.

items.stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
items.answer: virtual, erect and of the same size
items.markingKey: (b) virtual, erect and of the same size.
options: virtual, inverted and of the same size
virtual, erect and of the same size

items.stem: The chemical symbol of carbon is:
items.answer: C
items.markingKey: (b) Carbon: C.

items.stem: Define a solid.
items.answer: A state of matter with a fixed shape and fixed volume, in which particles are tightly packed
items.markingKey: (c) A state of matter with a fixed shape and fixed volume, in which particles are tightly packed. 1 mark: A solid – a state of matter with a fixed shape and fixed volume, in which particles are tightly packed.
options: Liquids and gases, which can flow
A state of matter with neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume, in which particles move freely
A state of matter with a fixed shape and fixed volume, in which particles are tightly packed
A state of matter with a fixed volume but no fixed shape, which takes the shape of its container

items.stem: Define the greenhouse effect.
items.answer: The trapping of heat near the Earth's surface by gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour
items.markingKey: (c) The trapping of heat near the Earth's surface by gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour. 1 mark: The greenhouse effect – the trapping of heat near the Earth's surface by gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour.
options: A layer of ozone gas in the stratosphere that absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun
The region around a star where a planet can have liquid water on its surface
The trapping of heat near the Earth's surface by gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour
The blanket of air that surrounds the Earth

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The coil of special wire, such as nichrome, in an appliance that becomes hot when current passes."
items.answer: a heating element
items.markingKey: (b) A heating element is the coil of special wire, such as nichrome, in an appliance that becomes hot when current passes.

items.stem: For a fair test of how the colour of a container affects how fast the water in it warms in sunlight, which of these must be kept the same?
items.answer: volume of water
items.markingKey: (a) Volume of water is a controlled variable; only the colour of the container is changed.

items.stem: The first person to observe and name cells, in a thin slice of cork, was:
items.answer: Robert Hooke
items.markingKey: (a) Robert Hooke observed cork cells in 1665 and called them cells.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A storm with lightning, thunder, strong winds and heavy rain, formed when warm moist air rises rapidly."
items.answer: a thunderstorm
items.markingKey: (c) A thunderstorm is a storm with lightning, thunder, strong winds and heavy rain, formed when warm moist air rises rapidly.

items.stem: Which of the following is a carnivore?
items.answer: frog
items.markingKey: (a) Frog is a carnivore. The others: pig – an omnivore; rabbit – a herbivore; mango tree – a producer.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A solution that contains a small amount of solute in a large amount of solvent."
items.answer: a dilute solution
items.markingKey: (d) A dilute solution is a solution that contains a small amount of solute in a large amount of solvent.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Rolling friction is less than sliding friction.
Reason (R): Luggage bags are fitted with wheels.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both true, but R is an application, not the explanation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Mosquito nets help to prevent malaria.
Reason (R): Malaria is spread by contaminated food.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A true; R false: spread by mosquito bites.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A sheet of paper does not form images.
Reason (R): Paper gives diffuse reflection because its surface is rough.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Water has a fixed boiling point.
Reason (R): Water is a compound.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Pure compounds have fixed boiling points; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Why does a solid have a fixed shape?
items.answer: Its particles are tightly packed with strong attraction and can only vibrate in fixed positions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: strong attraction. 1 mark: fixed positions.

items.stem: Why is Venus very hot though Mercury is closer to the Sun?
items.answer: Venus has a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat by a strong greenhouse effect.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: thick CO₂ atmosphere. 1 mark: greenhouse effect.

items.stem: Why is insulated wire used to make the coil of an electromagnet?
items.answer: So that current flows through the whole length of the coil instead of jumping between touching turns.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: prevents short between turns. 1 mark: current through all turns.

items.stem: Explain the difference between an observation and an inference with one example.
items.answer: An observation is what we notice with our senses (the road is wet); an inference is an explanation drawn from it (it rained).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: difference. 1 mark: correct example pair.

items.stem: A cell appears 5 mm long when seen through a microscope with a 10× eyepiece and a 10× objective. What is its actual length?
items.markingKey: Magnification = 10 × 10 = 100. Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05 mm.

items.stem: Why are people living near the coast moved to cyclone shelters before a cyclone hits?
items.answer: Strong winds, heavy rain and storm surges can flood low-lying coastal areas and destroy houses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: storm surge/flooding. 1 mark: wind damage.

items.stem: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle, the grass store 50 000 J of energy. If only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, how much energy reaches the frog?
Ananya dissolves 20 g of sugar in 180 g of water. Riya dissolves 30 g of sugar in 170 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.answer: Riya's solution
items.markingKey: Ananya: 20/200 × 100 = 10%; Riya: 30/200 × 100 = 15%. Riya's is more concentrated.

items.stem: Imran has a mass of 54 kg. Find Imran's weight on the Earth and on the Moon (g = 9.8 m/s²; gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth). What is the mass on the Moon?
items.answer: Earth: 529.2 N; Moon: about 88.2 N; mass stays 54 kg.
items.markingKey: W = 54 × 9.8 = 529.2 N; on Moon 529.2 ÷ 6 ≈ 88.2 N; mass does not change.

items.stem: A ray of light makes an angle of 35° with the surface of a plane mirror. Find the angle of incidence and the angle between the incident and reflected rays.
items.answer: Angle of incidence 55°; angle between rays 110°
items.markingKey: Angles are measured from the normal: i = 90° − 35° = 55°; r = 55°; angle between rays = 55 + 55 = 110°.

items.stem: Rahul heated naphthalene from 58 °C and recorded the temperature every minute. The temperature rose steadily, stayed at 80 °C for 4 minutes, and then rose again. (i) What is the melting point? (ii) Why did the temperature stay constant? (iii) What is the state of the substance during the constant part?
items.answer: (i) 80 °C. (ii) Heat was used to overcome interparticle attraction (melting), not to raise temperature. (iii) A mixture of solid and liquid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: A school roof in Chennai has an area of 150 m² and the city receives 600 mm of rain in a year. About how many litres of rainwater could be harvested in a year? (1 m³ = 1000 L)
items.answer: 90000 litres
items.markingKey: Volume = area × rainfall = 150 m² × 0.6 m = 90 m³ = 90000 L.

items.stem: List three safety rules for using electricity at home and give the reason for each.
items.answer: Do not touch switches with wet hands (water conducts); do not overload sockets (wires overheat); use ISI-marked appliances and earthing (prevents shocks); switch off mains before repairs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per rule with reason (max 3).

items.stem: A class recorded the time taken for 5 g of sugar to dissolve in 100 mL of water at different temperatures: 30 °C – 153 s; 40 °C – 121 s; 50 °C – 94 s; 70 °C – 61 s. (i) Name the independent and dependent variables. (ii) What pattern do you see? (iii) Predict the time at a temperature higher than 70 °C.
items.answer: (i) Independent: water temperature; dependent: time to dissolve. (ii) The higher the temperature, the less time sugar takes to dissolve. (iii) Less than 61 s.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: Rahul studied the growth of bacteria in a nutrient broth at 30 °C. The count was 20 at the start, 40 after 20 min, 80 after 40 min and 160 after 60 min.
(i) How long do the bacteria take to double? (ii) Predict the count after 80 min. (iii) Would growth be faster or slower at 37 °C (warm room)? (iv) Use this to explain why cooked food should be refrigerated.
items.answer: (i) 20 min. (ii) 320. (iii) Faster (near body temperature). (iv) Cold slows bacterial multiplication, so food stays safe longer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: Siddharth, of weight 600 N, stands in soft snow in Gulmarg. The total area of the soles of the boots is 0.025 m², and the total area of a pair of skis is 0.4 m².
(i) Find the pressure on the snow with boots. (ii) Find the pressure with skis. (iii) In which case will Siddharth sink less, and why? (iv) Give one other example where a larger area is used to reduce pressure.
items.answer: (i) 24000 Pa. (ii) 1500 Pa. (iii) With skis: the same weight acts on a larger area, so pressure is less. (iv) Wide straps of school bags / broad tyres of tractors / camel's broad feet.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Describe the water cycle and the carbon cycle with the main processes in each. How do human activities disturb these cycles?
items.answer: Water: evaporation from water bodies, transpiration from plants, condensation into clouds, precipitation, run-off and groundwater. Carbon: CO₂ taken in by photosynthesis, returned by respiration, decomposition and combustion; stored in fossil fuels and oceans. Humans: deforestation and burning fossil fuels raise CO₂; paving land reduces groundwater recharge.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each cycle; 1 mark human impact.

items.stem: Distinguish between communicable and non-communicable diseases with two examples of each. Explain how a mosquito-borne disease spreads and suggest three ways to control it.
items.answer: Communicable: spread from person to person by pathogens (malaria, tuberculosis). Non-communicable: do not spread; caused by lifestyle/heredity (diabetes, hypertension). Malaria: female Anopheles bites an infected person, picks up Plasmodium and passes it to a healthy person. Control: remove stagnant water, use nets and repellents, spray larvicides.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: distinction with examples; 1 mark: spread; 2 marks: control measures.

items.stem: Compare concave and convex mirrors and convex and concave lenses: the nature of images each can form and two uses of each.
items.answer: Concave mirror: real inverted (object far) or virtual erect enlarged (object close); torch reflector, shaving mirror. Convex mirror: virtual, erect, diminished; rear-view mirror, shop security. Convex lens: real inverted or virtual enlarged; magnifier, camera. Concave lens: virtual, erect, diminished; spectacles for myopia, door viewer.
items.markingKey: 1¼ marks for each device (images and uses).
